notes: Extra-hours advice now uses the take-home rate on one more hour, not the paycheck's average rate: a flat per-check fee (like the membership fee) doesn't grow when you add hours, so it no longer drags the advice down — a 16.75-hour week at $16/hr with $35/check in flat fees used to show +5 hrs as $48.63/week instead of $59.08, and a $100/month shortfall as 2.37 extra hrs/week instead of 1.95. The Paycheck tab's what-if and both goal tabs' 'add hours' lines use the same corrected rate. Averages for the week you already worked are unchanged.
